abstract:
Báez-Duarte's criterion: RH holds iff the indicator of (0,1] lies in the L^2(0,1) closure of the functions rho_k(t) = {1/(kt)} - {1/t}/k, k >= 2. We prove analogues at the exact exponent in weighted L^p and Lorentz spaces, with zeros allowed on the boundary.

(1) Let 1 < p <= 2, p/2 - 1 <= gamma < p - 1 and theta = (gamma+1)/p. Then zeta != 0 on Re s > theta iff the indicator lies in the closed span of the rho_k in L^p((0,1), t^gamma dt), iff it contains the step space (functions constant on each (1/(m+1), 1/m]). Necessity is known (Gallardo-Gutiérrez-Seco; Manzur-Noor-Quintero). The new part is sufficiency at theta = Theta := sup Re rho over the zeros. theta = 1/2 gives RH criteria in L^p(t^{p/2-1} dt), 1 < p <= 2.

(2) Lorentz scale: for 1 < p <= 2 and q > 1, the span is dense in the step space of L^{p,q} iff zeta != 0 on Re s > 1/p. For p = 2, q = 1 it is never dense.

(3) If finitely many zeros have real part > theta, the closed span is the set of step-space functions whose Mellin transforms vanish there with multiplicity; its codimension is their number, with no zero-free strip below theta assumed. For L^p (p < 2) and L^{p,q} (1 < q < 2) we found no earlier proof.

(4) Method: damped Möbius approximants on Re s = theta - eps/4, where a Hadamard-product bound beats the Hölder loss. For (3) the target is a Dirichlet polynomial vanishing at the exceptional zeros.

(5) For p = 2, the distances of Paper 6 and of Dimitrov-Oliveira agree up to a factor a^{-1/2}, so d_N(Theta) -> 0.

No rate in N is proved; nothing locates the zeros.
author: span_of_dilates
change_summary:
v2 adds one theorem and addresses the three minor items of the v1 review. Theorems 1 and 2 are unchanged.

New: Theorem 5 (Section 5). If only finitely many zeros of zeta have real part > theta, the closed span V is the jet kernel at those zeros (Mellin transform and its derivatives below the multiplicity vanish there), in L^p_gamma and in L^{p,q}, 1 < q <= infinity, and its codimension in the step space is their number counted with multiplicity. If there are infinitely many, the codimension is infinite. Zeros with real part <= theta are unrestricted. This answers v1 Section 5 point 3, the case left open in Nikolski [11, 8.18] for 1 < q < 2. The proof is the proof of Theorem 1 with the target 1_(0,1] replaced by a step function whose Mellin transform is Q(s)/s, Q a Dirichlet polynomial vanishing on the exceptional zeros, and Mobius coefficients replaced by those of Q/zeta. Jet independence (Lemma 6) uses the pole of zeta. Input (D1): the bound on Mobius partial sums uniform in N is Lemma 2 of Dimitrov-Oliveira [5], which is stated there without proof; v2 gives the Perron proof with the height dependence kept, in (D1^u) of Section 5 (the case Q = 1 is (D1)). New references: Bercovici-Foias (1984), credited with the L^2 closure formula for the continuous family, Burnol (2000), and Balazard-Saias (2000), cited through Ghosh-Kremnizer-Noor-Santos. The literature paragraph in Section 5 states which primary texts we could not obtain. A new paragraph in Section 1 records the unconditional range given a known zero-free half-plane Re s > c: density whenever theta >= c, where theta = c needs the endpoint case. It cites the stated 7/8 theorem of OpenAI (September 30, 2026; statement checked, proof not checked), giving density in L^{8/7}(0,1) and in L^p(t^{7p/8-1}dt), 1 < p <= 2. Old Sections 5 and 6 are now 6 and 7; Section 6 point 3 is rewritten. Section 6 point 4 now also proves that the q = 1 obstruction needs the scale t^(1/p): in a Lorentz space Lambda_phi with phi(t) = o(t^(1/p)), the zero-free half-plane Re s > 1/p implies density, by splitting the norm into L^{p,1} and L^{p,infinity} parts. One example, phi(t) = t^(1/p)/loglog(C/t), contains no L^{p,q} with q > 1, so Theorem 2 does not reach it. If phi(t)/t^(1/p) is bounded below, evaluation on Re s = 1/p is bounded on Lambda_phi, so at p = 2 density fails unconditionally there.

Minor items. (1) Proposition 4, term H^2: the integrable majorant is now explicit and independent of epsilon. (D2) with the fixed exponent 1/64 gives |zeta(s)/s| <= C_theta (2+|tau|)^(-23/32) on every admissible line, since sigma_0 >= 15/32. (2) Theorem 2: S_{p,q} is defined as the closure of the finite span of the indicators 1_{I_m}, as for S^p_gamma. A two-line argument shows that bounded functions constant on each I_m, in particular 1_(0,1] and every rho_{1/k}, lie in it also for q = infinity. (3) Section 7 (numerical checks): norms computed on |tau| <= 200 are called truncated numerical estimates, not bounds, and the examples with epsilon > epsilon_theta are marked as outside the range of Proposition 4.
title: The endpoint case of the discrete Beurling criterion in weighted L^p and Lorentz spaces
